question: In the DX-Scorecard MBR builder, does the "Refresh-all" / re-pull action (automated KPIs only) run inline within the builder with per-row Collecting/✓ chips, or route back through the standalone collection screen, and should its indeterminate progress strip plus "11 of 14" warning live inside the amber warning box exactly as the mockup shows?
recommendation: Route the automated (auto-only) re-pull through the standalone collection screen (UpdateKpisView), which already owns the per-row Collecting/✓ state chips and the indeterminate progress strip; do NOT build a second chip pipeline inside the MBR builder. And do NOT nest the progress strip inside the amber warning box — keep the "11 of 14" (N-of-M) automation warning in its own amber warn-line and render the indeterminate strip as a separate sibling below the action bar, exactly as the mockup lays them out.
supporting_points: The rich per-row experience (state-chip 'Collecting…' → success '✓', plus the indeterminate .update-progress bar and the amber .warn-line N-of-M automation warning) lives in UpdateKpisView/update-kpis.html, not in MbrBuilderView. The builder's own 'Refresh all data'/per-KPI refresh (refreshMbr via POST /__mbr/refresh) is coarse: a single shared `busy` flag plus a text status message — no per-row chips — so the auto-only per-row re-pull belongs to the standalone collection screen.

In both the mockup (update-kpis.html) and the React implementation, the amber warning box (.warn-line, warning-triangle icon in #d29922) and the indeterminate progress strip (.update-progress / #progress) are distinct sibling elements: the warn-line carries only the 'N of M' text warning and sits above the action bar, while the strip sits below it. They are never combined, so the strip should not live inside the amber box.

The '11 of 14'-style figure is the automatable-vs-total count for that warning line (automatableCount of totalKpis), independent of the running progress indicator; keeping the count in the warn-line and the spinner/bar in the separate progress strip matches the mockup and avoids conflating a static advisory with live sweep state.
